title: Tiny PR review playbook & rapid checklist
content:
Purpose:
Quick, bite-sized checklist and heuristics I use when I’m doing fast reviews (<= 10 files, < 200 LOC) or triaging refactor follow-ups. Meant for my own notes but shareable with others. Not a formal policy — keep it pragmatic.

Quick mental model: think about surface area (who will be affected), correctness (tests + edge cases), maintainability (readability + comments), and observability (metrics/logs/errors).

Fast PR triage workflow (2–10 min pass):
- Scan title/description: does it explain the why? If not, ask for 1–2 line context.
- Files changed: glance at filenames — are they cross-cutting (core/runtime/config)? If yes, escalate to deeper review.
- Run tests locally (if tiny): `pytest path/to/changed` or `pnpm test` smoke. If flaky, note flakes in comment.
- Diff skim for surprising changes: non-obvious config, SQL, migrations, or proto/schema changes.
- Quick run through checklist below — leave focused comments, not essays.

Rapid checklist (checkboxes I paste in PR comments):
- [ ] Does description include a minimal repro / example?
- [ ] Are API/contract changes called out and documented?
- [ ] Any migrations/rollouts needed? (DB, feature flags)
- [ ] Tests added/updated for new behavior? (unit + integration where applicable)
- [ ] Edge cases handled (empty input, large batch, partial failure)
- [ ] Logging/metrics traces added for new failure modes
- [ ] Any security-sensitive change? (auth, secrets) — flag immediately
- [ ] Backwards-compatibility: old clients/versions safe?

Heuristics for quick decisions:
- Minor refactor (rename, move short function) + no behavior change + tests pass => approve w/ small note.
- Adding a new config knob: expect integration tests/feature-flag plan + docs.
- Changes touching the serving runtime or batching code: request at least one reviewer from eng-serving-runtime and mention load test plan.
- If PR touches `console` UI and backend in same PR: prefer split unless the change is tiny and obvious.

Refactor follow-ups (notes I scribble while reviewing):
- Inline technical debt comment samples — e.g., move helper X into util/shared if referenced in 3+ places.
- Flag TODOs with `// TODO(evelyn): reason + ticket`. Convert long TODO lists into a single tracking ticket.
- If seeing repeated `if (isLegacy) { ... }`, suggest a small migration plan: deprecate flag, timeline, rollout milestones.

Observability / rollout quick checks:
- Did author add a metric or log for the new error path? If not, ask for at least an info-level log with context id.
- For changes that can affect latency (hot loop, serialization): request a microbenchmark locally (script + numbers).
- Canary/rollout: attach a short rollback plan in PR description if the change is risky.

Security & secrets guidance (fast):
- No secrets in code. If secret needed, point to KMS/K/V pattern and ask for a ticket with access plan.
- For auth surface changes, require at least one security reviewer (tag `@security`).

Comment style I try to use:
- Short, prescriptive: `Suggest: X` or `Consider: Y` rather than long rationale unless necessary.
- When blocking, give a clear next step: `Block until:` + short list.
- If non-blocking, mark `nit:` or `opt:` and give a reason.

Templates I paste into PR reply for small approvals:
- `LGTM` only when tests + basic checklist OK. Add short note of what you verified.
- `Approve with nit:` + single-sentence nit.

Common follow-up TODOs I create as issues from reviews:
- Consolidate `XXX` helpers in `pkg/common` (low effort) — ticket: DEV-###
- Add smoke test for `embedding` endpoint for 1k tokens (intermittent failure observed)
- Add docs for `batching.strategy` config (owner: infra)

Examples (snippets I keep):
- Minimal reproducible example request to ask for:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"hello world","max_tokens":8}'
```
- Minimal rollback plan snippet: `Rollback: revert to commit <sha>, redeploy route v1, scale to previous replica count. Estimated 10–15 min.`

Rough checklist for micro-performance concerns:
- Are any O(N^2) operations introduced on request path? (scan loops inside loops)
- Are large allocations (copying whole payload) happening? Suggest streaming or chunking.
- Any synchronous blocking IO on hot path? Flag for async or background worker.

Odds & ends — reminders to self:
- When in doubt, request a demo for non-trivial UX/behavior changes.
- Keep PRs small. If diff grows > 300 LOC, ask author to split logical concerns.
- If an author rebases a lot, encourage them to use small merge commits to preserve reviewability.

Open questions I sometimes leave in review comments (and why):
- "What is the expected error rate after this change?" — want to know whether we should alarm on it.
- "Which version clients will be impacted?" — to assess rollout strategy.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Turn recurring TODOs into `eng-developer-experience` checklist in Confluence.
- Share a pared-down version as a README template for new reviewers.

Status: draft — continues to evolve with feedback.

Notes-to-self: shave repetitions, add examples of good vs bad PR descriptions, collect 3 examples of risky diffs and how we handled rollbacks.
